the negative polarization observed for the comets at heliocentric distances greater than 3 AU can be explained in terms of the presence of submicrometer ice particles in cometary atmospheres.

the negative polarization of the scattered light in the atmospheres of distant (heliocentric distance > 3 AU) comets is caused by the presence of a significant fraction of submicrometer particles in the form either of spheroids or of aggregates composed of sub-micrometer spherical monomers.

the polarization of scattered sunlight by cometary atmospheres can be used to retrieve information about the size distribution and composition of cometary dust particles, including the presence of organic compounds.
